passage:
Sunday. Three colleagues have new cars and a fourth just came back from a beach holiday. Nazia said, "We're behind, aren't we?" and I said, "A bit." So this quarter we upgraded the phones, booked the beach trip and leased a car. I never opened the budget sheet. Tonight the card app showed the balance and my stomach dropped. It's the second card we've had to use in three months. We argued for an hour over whose idea it was, and both of us said, "You started it." I don't even like the car that much. I keep picturing our friends' photos, and I have no idea what their finances look like. Tomorrow I'll open the sheet.

Pradeep

qa.q: How many cards have Pradeep and Nazia had to use in three months?
qa.a: They have had to use the second card in three months.

qa.q: How does Pradeep feel when the card app shows the balance?
qa.a: Pradeep feels anxious and regretful, with a dropping stomach, and admits not even liking the car much.

qa.q: What else could Pradeep and Nazia do before spending again, and why?
qa.a: They could check their own budget sheet together before any purchase, because a plan built on friends' lifestyles ignores their own income.

qa.q: How might Nazia have felt during the hour-long argument?
qa.a: Nazia was probably tense and defensive, and stressed about the balance, since both of them said, "You started it."

grounding: Illustrates a couple raising their spending after seeing colleagues' cars and holidays without checking their own budget, ending up on credit cards and arguing.

passage:
Damini: did you see Nishant's photos? Bali. again
Bhupen: and Asha from my team just got a new SUV
Damini: we should do something too. we both earn decently
Bhupen: ok let's book that resort in Coorg. and the big TV
Damini: yes!! 🎉
(four months later)
Damini: card bill came. it's more than my salary
Bhupen: mine too. we only paid the minimum last month
Damini: what?? you said you'd handle it
Bhupen: I said I'd pay it. I didn't say I could
Damini: we never even checked what we could afford. we just looked at everyone else
Bhupen: can we not fight again tonight? that's the third time this week
Damini: I don't want to fight either. I just feel sick looking at this
Bhupen: let's sit down this weekend, look at everything, and maybe talk to someone at the bank about options

qa.q: What did Asha from Bhupen's team just get?
How does Damini feel looking at the card bill?
qa.a: Damini feels sick and anxious, realising they spent by comparing with others instead of checking their own budget.

qa.q: Which approach would suit Damini and Bhupen better than matching friends' lifestyles?
qa.a: They could lay out their own income and costs together and decide what they can afford before booking trips or big purchases.

qa.q: How is Bhupen affected by the choices they made?
qa.a: Bhupen feels worn down by the repeated fights and the unpaid balance, and wants to stop arguing and find a way forward.

grounding: It shows a couple raising their spending to match colleagues without checking their own budget, then relying on credit cards and arguing frequently.

passage:
In the small town of Sirsi, everyone knew when a family bought something new. When the Hegde family next door got a car, Deepak's mother mentioned it twice at dinner. When Sabina's colleague at the school went to Kerala for a holiday, the staff room talked about it for a week.
So Deepak and Sabina bought a scooter on instalments, then a big fridge, then took a trip to Goa on the credit card. They never sat down to see if their two salaries, his at the cooperative bank and hers at the school, could carry it all.
By the monsoon, the card bills were arriving faster than the salaries. They paid one card with another.
The quarrels started small, about who had wanted the fridge. Then they happened almost every night. Their little son started going quiet whenever the phone rang.
One evening Sabina sat on the step with the bills and simply cried.

qa.q: Where did Sabina's colleague go for a holiday?
What was Sabina feeling when she sat on the step with the bills?
qa.a: She felt overwhelmed and hopeless, crying because the spending had turned into debt and nightly quarrels.

qa.q: What would you change first in Deepak and Sabina's approach?
qa.a: Sit down together with both salaries and decide what they can actually afford, and speak to someone qualified at the bank about the card debt.

qa.q: How is the couple's little son affected?
qa.a: Their son has become anxious, going quiet whenever the phone rings because of the tension at home.

grounding: It shows a couple raising their spending to keep up with neighbours and colleagues without checking their budget, then depending on credit cards and arguing often.
